title: Only Colour, Not Yet a Flower
logline: At a flower market before dawn, buyers sort and price by colour in the half-light, before the flowers' names or uses matter at all.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From signals at the edge of sight in the dark to the half-light of a pre-dawn flower market, where colour is seen before any flower is named.

thread_out.thread: The instant before naming carries into a town's three-wheeler stand, where a driver's eyes turn to each passer-by and a judgement forms before anyone speaks.

requirements: An active pre-dawn flower market supplying temples
Low-light filming capability without disrupting the market's pace
Consent from sellers and buyers to film real trading

suggestions.name: Kandy's flower market district
suggestions.why: Kandy's temple culture, especially around the Temple of the Tooth, sustains active daily flower trading.
suggestions.season_notes: Poya days would see higher volume and different pressures.
suggestions.access_notes: Very early morning filming would need vendor cooperation and safe low-light conditions.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The eye does not see 'a marigold'; it meets colour, and the name, the kind and the value are added a moment later from what we have seen before. A buyer's fast judgement in the half-light starts with colour alone.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ඇසට පෙනෙන්නේ 'මල' නොව පැහැය පමණයි; එය කුමන මලද, කොතරම් හොඳද යන්න හඳුනාගන්නේ කලින් දැක පුරුදු දේ අනුව ඉන් පසුවයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches that the eye meets only colour, a blend of the colours of many tiny material clusters, and that knowing 'I saw such-and-such a thing' comes from marks learned in earlier seeing (C036). The bare moment of seeing is one of the rootless minds: it is weak, its feeling is neutral because colour touches the eye's sensitivity only lightly, and it needs light as well as a working eye, an object and attention (C009). The eye-door itself is a fine sensitivity inside the eye, not the visible eyeball (C035).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Before dawn the market works by lamp and first light, and the camera stays close to hands sorting by colour faster than anyone could name the flowers. As the light grows and bundles are priced, argued over and carried off to temples, names and values take over, and the viewer can feel the difference between that first glance and everything added to it.
lesson.caution: This is not 'perception is an illusion': in the texts colour is a real event, and only the named 'thing' assembled from it is a convention.
lesson.builds_on: The lagoon showed how little of what arrives ever registers; this film looks at what does register and finds that even a clear sight begins as bare colour, before anything is named.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
